column3: The image is the full F0-F5/F1 composition, linked by `ctrl_srp_image.py --with-aecp --layout split` with an 8 KiB stack.
It holds the descriptor image (7,512 / 19,520 B), the shape's `nvm_stage` and the lwSRP pool.
The stage was 3,344 / 13,264 B in KLJ2 and is 3,454 / 13,594 B in the split's KLJ3 (#823): ten-byte record headers.
The ledger at lane S1's face writer (#665) is planned by `ctrl_memory.plan`.
| Point | `rom` need, B | `sram` need, B | Planned RAMB36 equivalents | Base `e76a755a` | Against the 56-RAMB36 budget |
| 8x8, two interfaces (largest) | 119,800 | 112,992 | 57.5 | 56.0 | **over by 1.5 tiles, owed to lane S14** |
The face writer adds 6,496 to 6,592 B of `rom` and 336 B of `sram` at each point.

Its `applied` acknowledgement path, as `989c9f53` built it, accounts for 392 to 400 B of that `rom` and 16 B of that `sram`; at 8x8 with one interface it doubles `rom`'s last bank to 4 KiB, half a tile.
The model in which acknowledged state is the only truth a controller sees (#665, 6421238472) adds 1,056 B of `rom` and 224 B of `sram` at every point, against `989c9f53`, which did not have it:

All 224 B of `sram` are the core's new state: the held response (`AECP_HELD_BYTES`, 122 B) with its interface, length and requester, the four recorded values, the noted change, the wait's deadline and its three flags.

Holding an expired lock by its owner until its release is applied, and refusing SET_SYSTEM_UNIQUE_ID as every change is while one waits, add 64 B more of `rom` and no `sram` at every point, against `6d2b77bb`.
The other three points keep their RAMB36 count: only at 8x8 with two interfaces do the added bytes cross a granule, in `rom`.
The shipping point has 24 B of `rom` left before its next granule would make it 37.5.
At 8x8 with two interfaces `rom`'s banks hold 119,800 B in 120,832 and `sram`'s 112,992 B in 114,688.
That is 57.5 RAMB36, a tile and a half over the budget, with 1,032 B of `rom` left before the next granule would make it 58.0.
Without this model the point had 104 B left at 57.0, so returning to 57.0 needs 1,016 B of `rom`.
- constant port tables in `aecp_face.c`, `aecp_mbx.c` and `ctrl_app_aecp.c`: 64 B of `rom`;
- IN_PROGRESS carrying the held SUCCESS body instead of re-answering the command: 64 B more.
Together they would leave 119,672 B, still 57.5.
The rulings of 2026-10-26 ledger this point as owed to S14: one tile (#665, 6412739248), then a tile and a half (#665, 6425357821).

**The flip's ROM criterion is the owner's [decision of 2026-11-12](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/665#issuecomment-6824896581)** (option A), which supersedes, for the flip only, the requirement of 56 RAMB36 or fewer at every point with S14 merged.
- the target platform's image may plan 60.0 RAMB36, capped at 60.5; its debt is 4.0 RAMB36, 16,384 B of cold code to move;

`ctrl_memory.LEDGERED` holds the platform's entry at 60.0 and the size fixture's at 59.0, its cap since the tiers' merge (#894), 58.5 before it by the [ruling of 2026-11-12](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/665#issuecomment-6831583372) on round 30's STOP (below), each refused half a tile past ([section 3](#3-named-refusals)).
The ledger at lane S2b's merge of S1's face writer (#665, `dev-soft-core` `f4c9ad4f`) is planned the same way.
| Point | `rom` need, B | `sram` need, B | Planned RAMB36 equivalents | Before the merge, `bf1773c0` | Against the 56-RAMB36 budget |
| 8x8, two interfaces (largest) | 118,584 | 111,696 | 56.5 | 55.0 | **over by half a tile**, within the 57.5 ledgered and owed to lane S14 |
The merge adds 6,264 to 6,376 B of `rom` and 336 B of `sram` at each point, the face writer's.
Each point plans half a tile under S1's own ledger above, and the largest a whole tile, because the branch's compactions (sections 11 to 13) are in both.
| Point | Base `rom` / `sram`, B | KLJ3 `rom` / `sram`, B | Delta, B | RAMB36, base to KLJ3 |
Every point stays within 56 RAMB36, and the ledgered point within its 57.5, with 296 B of `rom` left before 58.0.
| Point | Platform `rom` / `sram` need, B | Platform RAMB36 | Fixture `rom` / `sram` need, B | Fixture RAMB36 | Platform minus fixture, B | Against the budget |
| 8x8, two interfaces (largest) | 125,048 / 113,936 | 59.0 | 119,824 / 113,008 | 57.5 | +5,224 / +928 | **over by 3.0 tiles, ledgered at 59.0, owed to lane S14** |
At 8x8 with two interfaces the platform's `rom` banks hold 125,048 B in 126,976 and its `sram` banks 113,936 B in 114,688.
That is 59.0 RAMB36, three tiles over the budget and a tile and a half over the fixture's 57.5.
It cannot reach 57.5 within the platform's files, because each region is planned in power-of-two banks of whole granules.
The fixture's own `sram` (113,008 B) already needs 28.0 tiles, so `rom` would have to fit 29.5 tiles (120,832 B).
That is a cut of 4,216 B from the platform's 5,224 B of `rom`.
The owner's ruling of 2026-10-29 (#665, 6505997821) ledgers that point at 59.0, owed to lane S14 under decision D3: the boot and the CSR policy are cold code, which D3 moves to flash.
Every other point stays within 56 RAMB36.
For the flip the owner's decision of 2026-11-12 (above) ledgers this point at 60.0, as ROM debt owed to S14.
| Point | Platform `rom` / `sram` need, B | Platform RAMB36 | Fixture `rom` / `sram` need, B | Fixture RAMB36 | Against the budget |
| 8x8, two interfaces (largest) | 124,480 / 112,672 | 58.5 | 119,264 / 111,744 | 57.0 | **over by 2.5 tiles**, within the 59.0 and the 57.5 ledgered, owed to lane S14 |

THE STEP (`ctrl_loop.h`, section 13) and SRP's one build a pass add 336 to 424 B of `rom` and 16 to 32 B of `sram` at each point; at 8x8 with two interfaces each image takes half a tile more than the round before's 58.0 and 56.5 (#665, 2026-11-02): the fixture's `rom`, 424 B more, one more 2 KiB bank, and the platform's `sram`, 32 B more than the 112,640 B its banks held exactly.

THE STEP's age limit, SRP's turn read before the poll's visits and the store's walk-free mark add 152 to 224 B of `rom` and up to 16 B of `sram` at each point (#665, 2026-11-03); only the platform's 1x1 two-interface image takes half a tile more, 41.5, its `rom` 216 B past the 110,592 B, 54 banks of 2 KiB, that it filled exactly.

`ctrl_plat` is 20,288 B at the largest point and 20,096 B before this branch's merge of the tsn-c-stack pin move (its 152 B in `app`, the struct padded to its 64-byte alignment); the ledger last named 19,968 B, a size the struct had already outgrown at round 27's head (20,096 B measured there), and 19,960 B before the age limit's two fields, 19,944 B before THE STEP's four fields and 21,240 B when the ledger above named it, so the ledger names the new size, as it requires when that struct changes.
Its size at each point is measured in the composed build by `ctrl_plat_image.py`: 17,472, 19,008, 18,112 and 20,288 B (`ctrl_memory_ledger.py`).
| Point | Fixture `rom` / `sram` need, B | Fixture RAMB36 | Platform `rom` / `sram` need, B | Platform RAMB36 | Platform `ctrl_plat`, B |

The size fixture's 8x8 image with two interfaces holds 123,112 B of `rom` in 124,928, 58.0 tiles, 1,816 B before its next granule, within the 58.0 its entry now ledgers ([section 3](#3-named-refusals)).

The platform's image at that point plans 59.5 tiles, within the 60.0 its entry ledgers by the owner's [decision of 2026-11-12](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/665#issuecomment-6824896581) (above): its `rom` needs 128,264 B in 129,024, 1,288 B past the 126,976 of its banks at the 59.0 of ruling 6505997821, and so did this branch's head before the merge (127,664 B) and round 27's (127,544 B).
Every link of that image since round 27 was refused first by a stale `ctrl_plat` size, so its tiles were not read, and no gate linked the platform image with its override.

[`plat_ledger.py`](../../tb/verilator/ctrl_split_boot/plat_ledger.py) now does, at every point: it links the platform's image against the split SoC's own maps with the override its point takes, and grades each image against the ledger, each check apart so that a stale key does not hide a plan past its tiles: the link, the image's `ctrl_plat` against `ctrl_memory_ledger.py`'s record and its override's key, and its plan against its override's tiles or the 56-RAMB36 budget, with every override of the platform's image linked at a point.

Seven planted ledgers must each be refused as they require: a stale key, a plan past its tiles, both at once, a stale record, the budget under a point's plan, the override not taken and an override no point links ([section 6](#6-reproduce)).

The CPU budget harness's 8x8/2if `answering-every-port` arm, the size fixture with a test port that answers every notice ([section 13](#the-polls-by-source)), is the image nearest its ledger: its build was refused once its `rom` passed 122,880 B, the granule past which the plan would take 58.0 tiles against the 57.5 then ledgered ([section 3](#3-named-refusals)) (#665, the [round 25 ruling](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/665#issuecomment-6751196896), item 5).
With the entry at 58.0 the granule is 124,928 B; at 58.5, the cap, the point's `rom` and `sram` banks are 124,928 and 114,688 B, and any further growth at that point is a STOP (below).
| Image | Arm's `rom`, B | Margin to the granule, B |
| This head with tsn-c-stack #32 at the pin (a scratch build, refused by the ledger) | 123,084 | 204 over |

The retry's rule added about 104 B of code, and with the two 1.5 KB buffers last every other field of the adapter is within a load's reach of its address, which takes 348 B of address arithmetic off `srp_mbx.o` (11,916 to 11,568 B of `.text`).
The other arms at `3a1d14c2`: `answering-later` 122,400 B, `answering-ports` 122,416 B, arm A 122,248 B.

Round 26's cuts ([section 13](#the-long-window-load)) add 80 B to arm A (122,328 B at this head) and to the arm: the notice's addressing in place, `same` and its calls, less the pool's two `memcpy` calls. tsn-c-stack #32 grows the core's `acmp.o` from 12,748 to 13,300 B of `.text`, so the pin move that carries it owes this arm 204 B of `rom`, or its next granule.

The owed-notice queue's slots each hold the largest legal AECPDU, 552 B (`AECP_OWED_BYTES`, the [ruling of 2026-11-13 on the owner's questions](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/894#issuecomment-6844175391) ([confirmed by the owner](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/894#issuecomment-6844947317)), option A), 16 of them at one interface (`AECP_MBX_OWED_SLOTS`), 6,144 B more `sram` there than 128 B slots took.

Where the count is 0, at two interfaces, the integrator names neither the slots nor the queue's operations (`aecp_owed_queue`), so the image links none of the queue's code: 200 B less `rom` in the size fixture's two-interface images and 208 B less in the platform's.

Each image, linked as `ctrl_srp_image.py` and `ctrl_plat_image.py` link it, against the caps (56 RAMB36 everywhere; at 8x8 with two interfaces the size fixture's 59.0 and the platform's 60.5), at the merge of #810's `084cf7a8` into the tiers with #904's map checks and THE PACE ([section 13](#the-tiers)):
| Point | Fixture `rom` / `sram` need, B, at the head (the ruling's head) | Fixture RAMB36 | Platform `rom` / `sram` need, B, at the head (the ruling's head) | Platform RAMB36 | Against the cap |

The size fixture's 8x8 image with two interfaces holds 125,792 B of `rom` in 126,976 at the head (125,200 at the ruling's head), past the 124,928 B that 58.5 holds, so its entry is 59.0 by the fallback of #894's [ruling of 2026-11-13](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/894#issuecomment-6844175391), item 2 ([section 3](#3-named-refusals)).
The platform's image there holds 130,328 B of `rom` in 131,072, 744 B before the granule its ledger's 60.0 holds.
The platform's 8x8 one-interface image plans exactly 56.0, which the budget accepts ([section 3](#3-named-refusals)); its `sram` needs 97,264 B in 98,304.

`ctrl_plat` is 17,536, 19,008, 18,176 and 20,288 B at the four points (`ctrl_memory_ledger.py`). #904's map checks and THE PACE added 480 to 488 B of `rom` at each point before the merge (`aecp_maps.c`, `aecp_mbx.c`), and the pace's stamp takes the tail padding of `struct aecp`, so no struct the ledger pins grows.

Before #810's merge the size fixture's images were 40.5, 41.0, 53.5 and 58.0 RAMB36 and the platform's 42.0, 43.0, 55.5 and 59.5 with #904's checks and THE PACE, and 40.0, 41.0, 53.5 and 58.0 and 42.0, 43.0, 55.5 and 59.5 without them; before the slots grew and the queue was compiled out, 38.5, 41.0, 52.0 and 58.0 and 40.5, 43.0, 54.0 and 59.5.
The five largest `.bss` objects at the shipping point are lwSRP's pool (9,920 B), the application (8,880 B), SRP (4,824 B), the descriptor image's values (4,527 B) and AECP (3,352 B).
At the largest point they are lwSRP's pool (48,064 B), F1's `nvm_stage` (13,264 B), the descriptor image's values (11,753 B), the application (10,064 B) and SRP (5,896 B).
The held open (`ctrl_app_open_held`) adds 24 B of `rom` and 16 B of `sram` to the fixture too; at the shipping point its `rom` then fills its last granule exactly, still 37.0.
| Point | `rom` need, B | `sram` need, B | Planned RAMB36 equivalents | As mapped RAMB36 / RAMB18 | As mapped tiles | LUT cells / FF | Byte floor |
The byte floor is the flat linked span at 4,096 B per RAMB36, rounded up.
Every point is within the 56-RAMB36 budget.
The largest leaves 2 tiles as mapped.
The budget check reads the planned 55.0, so its banks can grow 4 KiB (1.0 tile) before it is refused; with the unused bytes inside them, 5,064 B.
- it trims a ROM bit column that is constant across a bank, so `16384x31` takes 15 RAMB36 and one RAMB18;
M8a-2's route weighs that share against at most 1.0 tile.
The firmware of `ce10328c`, on dev `ac2c5e77`, planned 35.0 / 38.0 / 48.5 / 54.5 and mapped 34.0 / 37.5 / 47.0 / 53.0 tiles at the same points.
Dev `c6bd08c6` added 1,792 B of `.text` and 264 B of `.bss` at the largest point, and its `rom` gained a fifth bank.
| Point | Fixture `rom` / `sram` need, B | Fixture RAMB36 | Platform `rom` / `sram` need, B | Platform RAMB36 | Platform `ctrl_plat`, B |

One plan moves: the fixture's 1x1 with two interfaces needs 56 B of `rom` past its three banks (106,496 B), so it takes a fourth of 2,048 B and plans 41.0, accepted (#665 issuecomment-6807277620; the owner's firmware block-RAM limit, 224 KB, covers it).
The tightest point is the fixture's 8x8 with one interface, 88 B of `rom` before its next granule.
| Point | Fixture `rom` / `sram` need, B | Fixture RAMB36 | Platform `rom` / `sram` need, B | Platform RAMB36 | Platform `ctrl_plat`, B |
The fixture's 8x8 with two interfaces had 288 B of `rom` left at 57.5; it needs 232 B past its five banks (120,832 B) and plans 58.0, its `rom` in four banks of 122,880 B.
The platform's 1x1 with one interface had 320 B left at 39.0; it needs 168 B past its four banks (110,592 B), takes a fifth of 2,048 B and plans 39.5.
On that branch both images carry the KLJ3 stage, `nvm_stage` of 3,454 / 13,594 B, and its own `ctrl_plat`, 21,392 B at the largest point.

The smallest margins at that merge are 288 B of `rom`, at the platform's 1x1 with two interfaces, and 16 B of `sram`, at the platform's 8x8 with two interfaces, whose next granule would plan 59.5 against the 59.0 its override held there.
| Point | Fixture `rom` / `sram` need, B | Fixture RAMB36 | Platform `rom` / `sram` need, B | Platform RAMB36 | Platform `ctrl_plat`, B |
| 8x8, two interfaces (largest) | 123,808 / 113,168 | 58.5, its ledger's cap | 128,960 / 114,160 | 59.5, within its 60.0 | 20,288 |
Both images carry the KLJ3 stage, so both overrides are keyed on `nvm_stage` of 13,594 B, and `ctrl_plat` is this branch's struct, unchanged by the merge at every point (`ctrl_memory_ledger.py`).

**The size fixture's 8x8 image with two interfaces plans 58.5 RAMB36, the cap of the owner's decision, and its entry ledgers 58.5** (the [ruling of 2026-11-12](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/665#issuecomment-6831583372) on round 30's STOP): its `rom` needs 123,808 B in 124,928, as at round 29's head (123,112 B in the same banks), and its `sram` 113,168 B, 528 B past the 112,640 B of the 55 granules round 29's 112,576 B filled, so `sram` takes a 56th granule.

The KLJ3 stage and the store's open bits add the `sram` (#823's own table: +576 B at that point); neither side plans past 58.0 alone, the pin move's branch because its `rom` (121,064 B) takes one granule fewer.

The half tile is ROM debt owed to S14 on top of the 58.0 allowance: 528 B of `sram` past 55 granules, which a firmware cut (928 B of `rom` or 528 B of `sram`) would recover, a design change outside a sync round.
The cap is now fully used: any further growth at that point, a granule of either region, is a STOP.
Every other point of both images is within its ledger, the platform's largest within its 60.0 and every other point within 56;
Before: the base image's BIOS ROM took 16 RAMB36 and its SRAM 2, measured at `e8454e27`.
One LiteX SRAM of the whole need of that revision's largest image, 221,728 B, took 64 RAMB36.
The ledger rows are in the [plan](MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md#firmware-and-block-ram-ledger): 114 tiles after the split's release.
